lines.trans: Phew! My heart nearly jumped over the courtyard tree!
It was only the bookshop owner next door bringing our mail!
Read the stamped city envelope she handed you, Nour.
'Public Heritage Café Review — Wednesday, three o'clock sharp.'
Thank goodness—not tonight! Read the checklist inside, Nour!
Item one: clear street sign and open courtyard access for neighbours.
Gate oiled, wooden sign painted—check.
Item two: bright, safe indoor seating with fresh hot tea and food.
Twelve chairs, clean windows, new copper wire—and two mystery white jars!
Label those jars right now before anyone sleeps, Nour.

words.gram: prep على + demonstrative ها + plural noun

lines.trans: Left spoon... sweet! Right spoon... salty as the sea! Big red labels on both!
Crisis averted! Everyone to bed—six o'clock comes fast!

lines.trans: Left spoon... sweet! Right spoon... salty as the sea! Big red labels on both!
Crisis averted! Everyone to bed—six o'clock comes fast!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Describes a place or thing that is safe; for people 'safe and sound' is سالم.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood here is safe at night.
These stairs are not safe for children.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: In everyday Amman speech, أزمة most often means heavy city traffic.

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
We arrived ten minutes before the traffic jam.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of أكل (to eat), used as the everyday word for 'food'.

examples.text: الأكل اليوم ريحته واصلة لآخر الشارع.
examples.trans: The aroma of today's food reaches all the way down the street.

examples.text: لا تنسى تجيب أكل معك عالرحلة.
examples.trans: Don't forget to bring food with you on the trip.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Detached object carrier إيا- used when a verb already has a bound indirect object pronoun (-ك).

examples.text: الكتاب هاد كتير مفيد، رح أعطيك إياه بكرة.
examples.trans: This book is very useful; I'll give it to you tomorrow.

examples.text: الهدية جاهزة وبدي أبعتلك إياها مع أختي.
examples.trans: The gift is ready and I want to send it to you with my sister.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Combines with الحمد as a natural everyday expression of relief.

examples.text: الحمد لله خلصنا كل الترتيبات قبل ما يوصلوا الضيوف.
examples.trans: Thank God we finished all the arrangements before the guests arrived.

examples.text: الله يعطيك العافية على الشغل الحلو هاد.
examples.trans: May God give you strength for this wonderful work.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Form VII passive/reflexive of حلّ (to solve), meaning 'it got resolved'.

examples.text: الحمد لله المشكلة انحلّت قبل ما تكبر.
examples.trans: Thank goodness the problem got solved before it grew bigger.

examples.text: العقدة بالخيط انحلّت بسهولة بس سحبتها.
examples.trans: The knot in the thread came undone easily once I pulled it.

meanings.note: Used in ملح بحر ('sea salt') as well as for the Mediterranean or Dead Sea.

examples.text: حطيت رشة صغيرة من ملح البحر فوق العجينة.
examples.trans: I put a tiny pinch of sea salt on top of the dough.

examples.text: هوا البحر بيجي لطيف ومنعش آخر النهار.
examples.trans: The sea breeze comes in gentle and refreshing late in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بنود.

examples.trans: Read clause four in the contract.
This clause protects the tenant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian all-purpose word for 'all set, fine, spot-on!'.

examples.trans: Everything has to be spot-on!
Alright, I can remember the sentences.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Active participle of جاب (to bring); Jordanian Arabic prefers participles for ongoing or resultant states.

examples.text: شو جايب معك بالكيس يا زيد؟
examples.trans: What have you got in the bag, Zaid?

examples.text: أمي جايبة كعك بالتمر من عند الجيران.
examples.trans: My mom is bringing date cookies over from the neighbors'.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; الحمد لله means 'thank goodness'.

examples.trans: Thank goodness everything is fine!
We arrived safely, thank goodness.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from داخل (inside), given the -ة ending to match قعدة.

examples.text: الجو برد برا، خلينا نقعد بالقعدة الداخلية.
examples.trans: It's cold outside; let's sit in the indoor seating area.

examples.text: الرحلة الداخلية للعقبة بتاخد أقل من ساعة بالطيارة.
examples.trans: The domestic flight to Aqaba takes less than an hour by plane.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسلاك.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a slight adjustment.
We checked the bell wire by the door.

سلّم.gloss: to greet; say hello; hand over

meanings.en: to greet; say hello; hand over
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسلم, بيسلم).

examples.trans: Give my regards to Salma in the kitchen!
We hand the suitcase over to its owner on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Feminine form of صاحب, used both for 'friend' and 'owner/proprietor' in construct phrases.

examples.text: صاحبة المحل ست لطيفة وبتساعد الكل.
examples.trans: The owner of the shop is a kind woman who helps everyone.

examples.text: هاي صاحبتي من أيام المدرسة، لسه بنتواصل كل أسبوع.
examples.trans: This is my friend from school days; we still keep in touch every week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضبط, بيضبط).

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six, Tariq.
The plan worked out one hundred percent!

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian number 12; gains the -ر ending when directly preceding a counted noun.

examples.text: الاجتماع ببلش الساعة طناعش الظهر تماماً.
examples.trans: The meeting starts at twelve noon sharp.

examples.text: اشتريت طناعشر كاسة شاي جديدة للضيوف.
examples.trans: I bought twelve new tea glasses for guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عامة, plural: عامين); الشارع العام means 'main street / public road'.

examples.text: عالشارع العام برا في ضجة سيارات.
examples.trans: Out on the main road there is traffic noise.
A public park near the quarter.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: A written list or a restaurant menu; with -i it is قائمتي, 'my list'.

examples.trans: I wrote the shopping list before the market.
May I have the menu?

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Noun meaning a street sign, shop sign, or banner, from لفت (to draw attention).

examples.text: علّقنا لافتة خشب مدهونة جديد فوق باب المقهى.
examples.trans: We hung a freshly painted wooden sign above the café door.

examples.text: اللافتة اللي عالشارع الرئيسي مبينة من بعيد.
examples.trans: The sign on the main street is visible from far away.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مالحة, plural: مالحين).

examples.trans: I brought a tub of salted butter by mistake!
The white cheese is salty and delicious.

meanings.note: From جهل (not to know); plural form agrees with the dual noun مرتبانين.

examples.text: لقينا مرتبانين مجهولين بالخزانة بدون أي ورقة عليهم.
examples.trans: We found two mystery jars in the cupboard with no label on them.

examples.text: رقم مجهول رنّ عليّ الصبح بس ما رديت.
examples.trans: An unknown number called me this morning, but I didn't answer.

meanings.note: Passive participle of ختم (to stamp/seal), modifying مغلف in definiteness and gender.

examples.text: وصل مغلّف مختوم من البلدية اليوم الصبح.
examples.trans: A stamped envelope from the municipality arrived this morning.

examples.text: لازم الورقة تكون مختومة بختم رسمي عشان يقبلوها.
examples.trans: The paper has to be stamped with an official seal for them to accept it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مداخل.

examples.trans: The guesthouse entrance is lit by a brass lantern.
We greeted the guests at the entrance.

meanings.note: From دهن (to paint); agrees in feminine gender with اللافتة.

examples.text: اللافتة مدهونة باللون الأخضر ومكتوب عليها بخط جميل.
examples.trans: The sign is painted green and written on in lovely calligraphy.

examples.text: لا تسند عالحيط لأنو لسه مدهون جديد.
examples.trans: Don't lean against the wall because it was just freshly painted.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of راجع (to review/check); commonly used for official inspections or follow-ups.

examples.text: عندي مراجعة بالدائرة الحكومية بكرا الساعة تسعة.
examples.trans: I have a follow-up inspection at the government office tomorrow at nine.

examples.text: بعد مراجعة الحسابات، لقينا إنو كل الأرقام مزبوطة.
examples.trans: After reviewing the accounts, we found that all the numbers were right.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine pantry word (also pronounced مرطبان) for glass storage jars (dual مرتبانين).

examples.text: حطيت مرتبانين قزاز كبار عالرف: واحد سكر وواحد ملح.
examples.trans: I put two big glass jars on the shelf: one sugar and one salt.

examples.text: لزقنا ملصق واضح على كل مرتبان بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck a clear label onto every jar in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Derived from زيت (oil) via Form II زيّت (to oil/lubricate hinges).

examples.text: المفصلات مزيّتة منيح وما عادت تطّلع صوت أبداً.
examples.trans: The hinges are well oiled and don't make a sound anymore.

examples.text: صينية الفرن مزيّتة وجاهزة عشان نحط فيها العجين.
examples.trans: The baking tray is oiled and ready for us to put the dough in.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine metathesis of ملعقة ('spoon'), placing the ع before the ل.

examples.text: حطّي معلقة صغيرة قرفة على وجه السحلب.
examples.trans: Put a teaspoon of cinnamon on top of the sahlab.

examples.text: نسيت أجيب المعلقة عشان أحرك الشاي فيها.
examples.trans: I forgot to bring the spoon to stir the tea with.

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: Formal/signboard Arabic word for 'café' (alongside conversational كافيه), ideal for painted signs.

examples.text: كتبنا عاللوحة: مقهى جنينة الغرفة تسعة.
examples.trans: We painted on the sign: Room Nine Garden Café.

examples.text: المقهى رح يفتح يوميا من الصبح للمسا.
examples.trans: The café will be open daily from morning till evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكتبات.

examples.trans: There are old bookshops in downtown Amman.
The public library is a quiet place to read.

meanings.note: Dual ملصقين ('the two labels'), plural ملصقات ('labels / stickers').

examples.text: نور كتبت ملصقات واضحة وكبيرة لكل المرتبانات.
examples.trans: Nour wrote big, clear labels for all the jars.

examples.text: تأكد إن الملصقين ناشفين قبل ما تمسك القزاز.
examples.trans: Make sure both labels are dry before you pick up the glass.

meanings.en: bright; radiant; lighting up the room
meanings.note: Form II active participle of نوّر ('to illuminate'); also a warm welcome: الدار منوّرة بوجودك!

examples.trans: His face looked radiant in the photo.
The house is bright today with your presence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنام, بينام).

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (ن-ط-ط) for jumping or hopping over an obstacle.

examples.text: القطة نطت عن الحيط للجنينة بهدوء.
examples.trans: The cat jumped quietly off the wall into the garden.

examples.text: ما بدنا الضيوف ينطوا فوق الكراسي بالممر!
examples.trans: We don't want guests climbing over chairs in the hallway!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of على النوم, used briskly to send everyone to bed.

examples.text: صار الوقت متأخر كتير، يلا عالنوم يا جماعة!
examples.trans: It's gotten really late—off to bed, everyone!

examples.text: النوم الكويس بالليل بعطيك نشاط طول اليوم.
examples.trans: Sleeping well at night gives you energy all day long.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
